The **risk rules v3.1 velocity threshold tuning** (CHG-0620) deployed on June 20, 2026 at 15:00 Sao Paulo time **fully recovered** Brazil's conversion rate after a sharp drop caused by overly aggressive risk rules two days earlier.[1]

### What Happened

On **June 18** at 09:00, a new card-velocity rule (CHG-0618, Risk rules v3) was deployed in Brazil that immediately caused conversion to drop by blocking too many legitimate payments.[1]

The June 20 tuning corrected this by adjusting the velocity threshold, bringing both conversion and risk block rates back to their pre-incident baseline levels.[2]

### Impact by Card Type**Brazil conversion before, during, and after the risk-rule tuning**

| period | card_type | payment_intents | approved | conversion_rate | blocked_by_risk | risk_block_rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before June 18 (baseline) | credit | 26901 | 23638 | 0.8787 | 336 | 0.0125 |
| Before June 18 (baseline) | debit | 10907 | 8571 | 0.7858 | 141 | 0.0129 |
| June 18-19 (drop) | credit | 3511 | 2991 | 0.8519 | 123 | 0.035 |
| June 18-19 (drop) | debit | 1416 | 1078 | 0.7613 | 51 | 0.036 |
| June 20+ (after tuning) | credit | 16434 | 14457 | 0.8797 | 241 | 0.0147 |
| June 20+ (after tuning) | debit | 6522 | 5130 | 0.7866 | 87 | 0.0133 |**Credit cards:**
- Baseline (before June 18): 87.9% conversion, 1.3% risk block rate
- Drop (June 18-19): 85.2% conversion, 3.5% risk block rate (2.7 pp drop)
- After tuning (June 20+): **87.9% conversion**, 1.5% risk block rate — **fully recovered**

**Debit cards:**
- Baseline (before June 18): 78.6% conversion, 1.3% risk block rate  
- Drop (June 18-19): 76.1% conversion, 3.6% risk block rate (2.5 pp drop)
- After tuning (June 20+): **78.7% conversion**, 1.3% risk block rate — **fully recovered**

The tuning reduced the risk block rate from the elevated 3.5-3.6% during the incident back to baseline levels of 1.3-1.5%, allowing legitimate payments to proceed while maintaining fraud protection.[2]

questions.question: During the issuer maintenance in Brazil on the morning of 21 July 2026, did retries on another acquirer recover the declined payments?

facts.K1: Barely, and they could not: issuer BR-ISS-03 was unavailable during its maintenance (EXT-0721, 12:00 to 15:00 UTC, 09:00 to 12:00 local time), so its payments failed on every acquirer, mostly with 91 (issuer or switch unavailable). Its failed first attempts were retried on another acquirer (52 of 52), but only 2 were recovered (about 4%), because a retry reaches the same issuer. The cause is issuer-side, and rerouting cannot avoid it.
facts.K2: In the same hours of the previous 14 days, about 31% of this issuer's retried payments were recovered (15 of 49) and its final approval was about 88%, against about 11% in the window.

## Retries During BR-ISS-03 Maintenance Were Attempted But Largely Ineffective

During the issuer maintenance window in Brazil on the morning of July 21, 2026 (09:00-12:00 local time), **retries on another acquirer were attempted but recovered very few declined payments**. The system cascaded 77 payments to a second acquirer but only recovered 15 of them, achieving just a **19.5% recovery rate** compared to the typical performance.[1]

### The Problem: Issuer-Side Outage

The maintenance affected **issuer BR-ISS-03**, which sent 56 payments during the window and experienced 52 first-attempt failures (92.9% failure rate).[2] The dominant decline code was **91 ("Issuer or switch unavailable")**, accounting for 45 of the 52 failures.[3]

**Why retries didn't help:** Code 91 indicates the issuer itself was unavailable. Since the card determines which issuer processes the payment, retrying on a different acquirer still routes to the same unavailable issuer (BR-ISS-03). This is an **issuer-side outage** — retries and rerouting cannot avoid it.**Decline codes from BR-ISS-03 during maintenance**

## Retries Were Attempted But Mostly Failed to Recover Payments

During the BR-ISS-03 issuer maintenance on the morning of July 21, 2026 (09:00-12:00 São Paulo time), **retries on another acquirer were attempted but recovered very few declined payments**. [1]

### Key Findings

**Cascade behavior worked, but recovery failed:**
- All 52 failures from BR-ISS-03 were retried (100% cascade rate)
- Only 2 of 52 retries succeeded (3.8% recovery rate of cascaded payments)
- This contrasts sharply with other issuers during the same window, which achieved 42.9% to 100% recovery rates when retries were attempted [2]

**The problem was issuer-specific:**
- BR-ISS-03 was undergoing scheduled maintenance, causing it to decline payments on **all acquirers**
- The most common decline was code 91 (issuer unavailable): 45 of 52 failures
- Retries couldn't help because the issuer itself was down—switching acquirers didn't change the outcome [3]

### Impact

The maintenance window caused:
- Final approval rate dropped to 72.2% (vs. 88.0% baseline), a decline of **15.9 percentage points**
- **56 lost approvals** out of 352 payments
- **$4,110 in lost approved volume**
- $502 in fees paid during the window [1]**BR-ISS-03 failures and cascade behavior during maintenance**

| issuer_id | first_acquirer_id | first_reason_code | failures | cascaded | recovered | cascade_rate | recovery_rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BR-ISS-03 | C | 91 | 36 | 36 | 2 | 1.0 | 0.0556 |
| BR-ISS-03 | A | 91 | 9 | 9 | 0 | 1.0 | 0.0 |
| BR-ISS-03 | A | 05 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 1.0 | 0.0 |
| BR-ISS-03 | C | 05 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 1.0 | 0.0 |
| BR-ISS-03 | A | 96 | 2 | 2 | 0 | 1.0 | 0.0 |
| BR-ISS-03 | C | 96 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 1.0 | 0.0 |### Why Retries Didn't Work

This was an **issuer-side outage**, not an acquirer-side problem. When an issuer is in maintenance:
- The card's issuing bank determines which issuer processes the authorization
- All acquirers route to the same issuer for that card
- Retrying on another acquirer still hits the same unavailable issuer
- Recovery is only possible if the issuer comes back online during the retry window

The cascade mechanism functioned correctly by attempting retries, but the nature of the incident—a scheduled issuer maintenance—meant those retries had nowhere to succeed.
